title: The more knobs your strategy has, the more likely it's memorizing the past, not finding an edge
author: zohaahmed1
selftext:
Learned this the slow way. Every parameter you add to a strategy makes the backtest look better and the live results worse, because more knobs means more ways to accidentally fit the model to the specific noise of your historical data instead of a real repeatable pattern.



A strategy with 2 or 3 parameters that works decently across many instruments and periods is far more trustworthy than one with 12 finely-tuned values that prints a perfect equity curve on one dataset. The perfect curve is usually the warning sign, not the goal.



The test I use now, change each parameter by a small amount and see if performance collapses. If nudging a value from 14 to 16 destroys it, it was fit to noise. Robust edges degrade gracefully, overfit ones fall off a cliff. And I model live costs pessimistically too, my backtest-to-live gap shrank once I stopped assuming perfect fills (running live on AvaTrade the real spread was nothing like my flat assumption).



How many parameters do you consider too many, and do you test parameter sensitivity or mostly go on out-of-sample results?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
the nudge test is the right instinct but it undercounts, because you're moving one knob at a time and the cliff usually lives in the interaction. two values that each degrade gracefully on their own can still fall off together.

the other thing nobody counts is the search itself. if you tried four hundred configurations and kept the best one, the selection is a parameter too, and it never shows up anywhere in the final strategy's knob count. that's why a 3 param strategy pulled out of a huge sweep can be just as fit to noise as a 12 param one you tuned by hand.

replies.author: tinfoil_powers
replies.body: So where do you get the edge? Seems like you're screwed either way

replies.author: greatestNothing
replies.body: you are. basically the only thing i've found that is worth repeating is coverage via multiple strategies and multiple accounts and multiple instruments.

comments.author: Puzzled-Job9556
comments.body: Currently developing a strategy from very little prior knowledge. Have 8 triggers and then an assessment of indicators. I'm not testing it on historical data and am testing it against a live market and will be amending on the results obtained over the next 6 months before starting to paper trade.
